checks.claim: On the Mercedes S-Class, the rear wheels turn opposite the front below about 60 km/h (37 mph) and the same way above that
checks.why: Motor1, Mercedesblog and CarExpert (and this round's search) put the switch to same-direction steering at about 60 km/h.

checks.claim: Mercedes S-Class rear-axle steering turns the rear wheels up to 10 degrees and cuts the turning circle by up to about 2 meters
checks.why: Mercedes press text: up to 10 degrees rear steering angle (the optional system, at low speed), turning circle up to 2 m smaller; the video says only 'about 10 degrees'.

sources.title: The new Mercedes-Benz S-Class - Mercedes-Benz USA media

checks.claim: Rear-wheel steering systems use an electric motor actuator on the rear axle to turn the rear wheels.
checks.why: ZF AKC and AISIN Active Rear Steering use electromechanical actuators on the rear axle; patents describe a motor turning a threaded drive that moves the steering rod.

checks.claim: The GMC Hummer EV's CrabWalk turns all four wheels the same way at low speed so the truck moves diagonally.
checks.why: GMC: CrabWalk turns the rear wheels at the same angle as the front at low speed; Cars.com: the vehicle moves diagonally.
